doc.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Roy Brooks and M'Boom
summary: Fuller and Brower talk of Roy Brooks's wild percussion, including playing a saw, and M'Boom.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: One of the drummers—it wasn’t Louis Hayes, I think it was the one that had all the trouble.

He followed Louis. He was really out there. You know what he could do? He could play-- he had this big saw, and he took a mallet from a vibraphone and he could play sort of like (imitates long sounding metallic notes). Oh man…

I used to work Montreux Detroit, And one year he did this thing called “Giant Steps” and he incorporated a guy dribbling a basketball, he incorporated a martial arts, he had cats playing Afro Brazilian, he had every… It was almost like M’Boom.
M’Boom, he started that. Max took that from him. M’Boom, that was Roy!
It was crazy what he did. It was almost like-­
